title: P46 (P.Mich. inv. 6238): Ephesians 6:8-Galatians 1:8 (fols. 80v-81r)
source: P46 (P.Mich. inv. 6238, University of Michigan Library): photographs as published in the INTF New Testament Virtual Manuscript Room; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P46; English from the King James Version
description: Ephesians 6:8-Galatians 1:8 in P46, the papyrus codex of Paul's letters copied around 200: fols. 80v-81r, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P46 is a papyrus codex of the letters of Paul copied in Egypt around 200, the oldest surviving collection of Paul's letters. 86 of its 104 leaves survive: 56 in the Chester Beatty Library, Dublin (Biblical Papyrus II, published by Frederic Kenyon in 1934-1937) and 30 in the University of Michigan Library, Ann Arbor (P.Mich. inv. 6238, published by Henry Sanders in 1935). The letters run in the order Romans, Hebrews, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Ephesians, Galatians, Philippians, Colossians and 1 Thessalonians; the first seven leaves (Romans 1:1-5:17) and the end of the book are lost. Hebrews standing after Romans, and the doxology of Romans (16:25-27) standing after 15:33, are among its best-known features.

Each section below is one page side: the holding library's photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse that has text on the page. The lower lines of many leaves are lost; the transcribers' restorations are in square brackets.

This entry covers fols. 80v-81r (Ephesians 6:8-Galatians 1:8).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>6:8</sup>Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free. <sup>9</sup>And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him. <sup>10</sup>Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. <sup>11</sup>Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. <sup>12</sup>For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, agains t the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. <sup>13</sup>Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. <sup>14</sup>Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; <sup>15</sup>And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; <sup>16</sup>Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. <sup>17</sup>And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God: <sup>18</sup>Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
translation.scan_note: University of Michigan Library photograph 10046x6238_157JP2_UMich.jpg (https://ntmss.info/images/webfriendly/10046/10046x6238_157JP2_UMich.jpg), linked to NTVMR page 1420 (folio 80v) in NTVMR's page index. 6:8 begins on the previous page. Checked on the image: the scribe's page number ρνζ (157) at the head of the page, continuing the sequence of the neighbouring pages.

translation.text: <sup>6:20</sup>For which I am an ambassador in bonds: that therein I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak. <sup>21</sup>But that ye also may know my affairs, and how I do, Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things: <sup>22</sup>Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that ye might know our affairs, and that he might comfort your hearts. <sup>23</sup>Peace be to the brethren, and love with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. <sup>24</sup>Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen. <sup>Galatians 1:1</sup>Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;) <sup>2</sup>And all the brethren which are with me, unto the churches of Galatia: <sup>3</sup>Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ, <sup>4</sup>Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father: <sup>5</sup>To whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. <sup>6</sup>I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: <sup>7</sup>Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ. <sup>8</sup>But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed.
